peak_definition.rule: A timestep is a peak if cpu_real >= P90(container_train)
peak_definition.threshold_application: Same train-fitted thresholds applied at training weighting and evaluation labelling

sequence_definitions.peak_sequence: A 96-step forecast horizon contains >= 1 peak timestep
sequence_definitions.evaluation_horizon: Day-1 validation horizon (first 96 val timesteps per container)

rejected_alternatives.reason: Too permissive (~22% train peak timesteps); weak spike semantics; minimal improvement in zero-peak sequence discrimination over P90
Conservative (~11% train peaks); may under-emphasize moderate surges; highest near-idle label distortion (37%) though better zero-peak sequence discrimination
Not adopted; Phase 2 exploration showed near-idle artefact affects 5/99 containers (5%); documented as limitation rather than modifying the percentile-based definition
Rejected; per-container MinMax scaling makes global thresholds misleading across heterogeneous workloads
Rejected for Phase 3; >92% of sequences are peak sequences under all percentiles (Task 3)

known_limitations: Five near-idle containers have zero thresholds, inflating peak labels (~29% of train peak timesteps at P90)
Spiky workload label partially reflects near-idle CV artefact
Validation peak rates exceed train rates under fixed thresholds (distribution shift)
Short train history (~614 steps/container) makes percentile estimates coarse for low-activity containers
